items.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: We worked with Bob Stewart in that big orchestra in Switzerland. Bob Stewart the tuba player.

ctx.x: First of all it started with the whole racial thing. Billie Holiday had to go through the kitchen in the hotel because she was black, and so on and so on. So that started it. Second, if you aren’t strong, and you become well known, and you are king on stage, and then you have to go home and pay your phone bill, you have to do the daily grind, and if you aren’t strong personally you will go on drugs. We worked with Bob Stewart in that big orchestra in Switzerland. Bob Stewart the tuba player.

In Switzerland. And a huge success. The orchestra was a huge success. And then we had to come out for three encores, went back to the dressing room and Bob Stewart said with a very sad voice, “Well I was for a moment king again. Now I’ll have to go home and see whether I have enough money to pay my bills.” So a lot of musicians could not deal with this. You know it started with the racial thing. It started with very, very little pay, long, long tours. Remember the start of Billie Holiday, she never wanted to go…
